concepts.title: Nutrition - Autotrophic and Heterotrophic
concepts.definition: Nutrition supplies the material and energy of life: autotrophs like green plants build food from carbon dioxide and water using sunlight in photosynthesis, while heterotrophs depend on ready-made food, digesting it stepwise as in the human alimentary canal or in amoeba's food vacuoles.
concepts.key_idea: Cook your own or consume others - autotrophs and heterotrophs cover both routes.
question_patterns: differentiate autotrophic and heterotrophic nutrition with examples

solution_steps.explain: Green plants cook their own food; animals consume ready food.
Ingestion, digestion, absorption, assimilation and egestion run in sequence.
Enzymes and organs specialise each step.

concepts.title: Respiration and Transport
concepts.definition: Respiration releases energy from food: aerobic breakdown in mitochondria yields the most energy, anaerobic breakdown in yeast or muscle yields less with alcohol or lactic acid; in humans the respiratory surface of alveoli loads oxygen onto blood, and the pumping heart with its vessels transports it everywhere, while plants move water upward through xylem using transpiration pull.
concepts.key_idea: Break food with oxygen, then carry it: alveoli exchange, heart pumps, xylem lifts.
question_patterns: differentiate aerobic and anaerobic respiration with products

solution_steps.explain: With oxygen energy is full; without it, alcohol or lactic acid forms.
Blood in animals and xylem-phloem in plants transport materials.
Alveoli for gases, capillaries for food and waste.

concepts.title: Excretion in Humans and Plants
concepts.definition: Excretion removes toxic wastes: in humans the kidneys filter blood in nephrons, returning useful substances and draining urine through ureters to the bladder; plants recycle or store wastes in leaves, bark and vacuoles, releasing some as resins and gums.
concepts.key_idea: Filter the blood, keep the useful, flush the toxic - the nephron's triple duty.
question_patterns: describe the structure and function of a nephron

solution_steps.explain: Blood enters the glomerulus where filtration begins.
Glucose, salts and water return to the blood in the tubule.
Remaining fluid drains as urine through the ureter to storage.
